local_articles.title: Irrepressible Sinner outlasts Zverev to win second straight Wimbledon title
local_articles.snippet: LONDON: Jannik Sinner was at his clinical best as he successfully defended his Wimbledon title with a bruising four-set victory over French Open champion Alexander Zverev in Sunday’s final. The world number one recovered from losing the first set in a match largely dominated by serve, eventually wearing Zverev down to secure a 6-7 (7/9), 7-6 (7/2), 6-3, 6-4 win. “You can feel the nerves on Sunday morning, it is a very special place,” said Sinner, who saved the only break point he faced on Center Court. “You never know how many times you are going to come back. I never take it for granted.” The Italian was rewarded for his perseverance in an attritional contest with his first Grand Slam title since lifting the trophy at the All England Club 12 months ago.
